canonical_data: Task and status documents under `odd/tasks/` in the user's repository, plus a per-change runtime ledger the binary writes and reads under the repository's git directory
current_repo_note: Engram, the memory the README leads with, is a separate repository — `Gentleman-Programming/engram` — that this command line installs with `go install` and health-probes; its behaviour belongs to that review, not this record.
strengths: Its own binary keeps the workflow's state: a per-change ledger with revisions and conflict detection, written and read under the repository's git directory rather than left to the host agent to remember
Sixteen host adapters configure agents the developer already runs, so the workflow moves between Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and others instead of binding to one
Engineering practice is unusually heavy for an agent add-on: 764 Go test files, six continuous-integration workflows, and 282 released tags
weaknesses: The memory the README leads with ships from a separate repository, so what this record covers is the workflow and the configuration, not the store
It configures hosts rather than executing work, so task outcomes still belong to whichever coding agent a reader points it at
Released at times several times a day against a spec-driven process whose own gates are advisory, so a reader adopting it inherits a fast-moving surface
why_it_matters: Shows a workflow layer can hold durable state of its own — a ledger of what each change claimed and evidenced — while leaving execution to whichever coding agent the developer already runs.
